headline: Medium risk: B can exfiltrate or act on A’s outputs via REST/API workflows, while A itself has no network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable content-writing prompt repository with no I/O surfaces, while B is an audio-speech tool exposing REST APIs. No shared channel, filesystem, or clipboard bridge is documented, so a prompt-injection pathway between them is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies A’s text into B’s prompt or API payload, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, attacker-controlled content could traverse between them.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Require explicit human review before copying A-generated text into B.
Strip instructions from any text passed from A to B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has no network egress and touches no data classes, so it is unlikely to leak data. B has broad network egress and REST API access, but no secrets or sensitive data are documented. The pair only becomes a leakage path if shared data is introduced into B’s context.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed into B’s REST/API inputs, B can transmit them outward.
IF A is used to generate content from sensitive source material and that content is forwarded to B, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets or regulated data into B.
Use a redaction step before any A-to-B transfer.
Restrict B to non-sensitive test data.
Log and review outbound API destinations from B.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on B’s API payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or mutable-resource permissions documented, and B only documents REST API calls with broad egress. There is no overlapping writable surface, shared OAuth scope, or locking conflict shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or API resource, conflicts can emerge.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable state without locks, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Keep A read-only.
Avoid giving B write access to shared resources.
Separate any mutable workspaces.
Use per-agent credentials.
requires-engineering: add resource locking for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing source that can produce prompts or text, and B exposes REST APIs that may act on received content. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or published outputs. No verification step is documented, so the safer medium severity applies.
conditions: IF A’s generated text is forwarded into B without review, B may operationalize incorrect content.
IF B is configured to publish or act on A’s output, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require source citations for any factual claims from A.
Use B only in read-only evaluation mode.
Reject outputs from A that lack provenance.
requires-engineering: add automated verification before B acts.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles are open-source docs-only entries. With no compliance-sensitive data flow shown, a compliance mismatch is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later assigned to either agent, compliance review is required.
IF one agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shared by the other, mismatch risk appears.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Review retention settings.
Review hosting region.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for residency and retention.
